targetAudience.primary: Engineering managers, platform engineers, and evaluation owners deploying agent-generated software
targetAudience.knowledgeAssumption: The reader understands repository tests, continuous integration, concurrency, resource limits, and deployment environments.
targetAudience.readerProblem: A rich plan-test-refine trace and passing local tests may be accepted as production readiness even though load, parallelism, memory pressure, or target topology has not been qualified.

whyNow: A reproducible agentic Julia and supercomputing study exposes failures that appear only as workload and parallelism increase, despite earlier functional success.

externalHook.description: Agent-generated implementations can pass small correctness tests and later deadlock, exhaust memory, crash, or time out under realistic execution conditions.

coreProposition: Functional success and a rich agent development trace are necessary but insufficient evidence of operational capability; stronger completion claims require a separate, risk-proportionate qualification gate over the relevant workload, concurrency, resource, topology, and reproducibility dimensions.

originalValue.description: Separates functional correctness, development-process evidence, operational failure envelope, performance/scalability evidence, and transfer/reproducibility evidence so each gate closes only the proposition it actually tested.

readerTakeaway: Label the evidence layer that passed, then add operational qualification only for the failure dimensions material to the intended deployment.

supported: The examined study uses iterative planning, generation, testing, repair, and performance experimentation rather than one-shot code generation.
The public research package exposes prompts, generated artifacts, interaction logs, tests, and runtime data.
Some generated implementations that passed small functional checks later encountered deadlock, oversubscription, out-of-memory failure, crash, or timeout at larger workloads or parallelism.
The evidence supports separating functional acceptance from operational qualification.
unsupported: A general ranking of programming frameworks
Guaranteed discovery of every operational failure
Direct transfer of Julia or supercomputing metrics to all enterprise software
Population-level model reliability from one generation per condition
uncertain: How many independent generations are needed for model-level reliability claims
Which target-environment facts should be exposed during refinement
How to avoid benchmark overfitting while improving operational evidence

firstPartyRole.rationale: The argument derives from independent public research and does not require a first-party project.

decisionReason: The study supplies a reproducible failure contrast and supports a practical completion-gate model while preserving transfer and sample-size limits.
